$comment: DRAFT ledger schema + worked example for issue #60. One director only (Akira Kurosawa). Not approved, not for app use until the owner signs off the roster, the method and the score-display licensing decision.
methodSummary: Owner decision 2026-11-13: films are ranked by IMDb and Rotten Tomatoes scores. Each film is ranked within this list by IMDb rating and by Tomatometer (ties share the average rank); the two ranks are averaged (ranks, never the raw scores); ties are broken by higher IMDb rating, then more IMDb votes. A Tomatometer with fewer than 10 reviews or no value is ignored and that film is ranked by IMDb alone (flagged rtUsed:false). The film selection is unchanged from the editorial research list; editorialRank keeps the earlier order. Scores are read online and dated, never estimated.

imdb.note: IMDb title pages returned HTTP 403 to the research fetcher, so ratings come from the official daily dataset instead. Dataset licence is personal / non-commercial use only; see licensing caveats in the markdown.

rt.source: Rotten Tomatoes film page, critics Tomatometer and its review count
rt.note: Read via an HTML-to-text fetcher, not by hand. Percentages for the ten films were cross-checked against the Kurosawa celebrity filmography table where it listed them. Review counts are live and change; treat as a dated snapshot.

films.title: Seven Samurai
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay).

rt.rtYearNote: RT lists the 1956 US release date.

films.rationale: Kurosawa's synthesis of epic scale, ensemble characterisation and kinetic multi-camera action editing set the template for the modern ensemble adventure, and it tops both the audience and critic evidence.

films.title: High and Low
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay).
films.rationale: A kidnap drama staged almost entirely in one apartment that then breaks into a procedural through Yokohama, turning a crime thriller into a study of class and conscience.

films.title: Ikiru
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay).

rt.rtYearNote: RT page showed 1956 (US release); its celebrity table and TMDB show 1952.

films.rationale: The most humane film in the canon: a dying clerk's search for meaning, structured around a bold shift into his wake, and carried by Takashi Shimura's performance.

films.title: Rashomon
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay).
films.rationale: Four irreconcilable testimonies of one crime made narrative subjectivity a formal subject and introduced Japanese cinema to the world (Golden Lion, Venice 1951); ranked above higher-scoring audience favourites because its directing innovation is the more consequential.

films.title: Stray Dog
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Writer).

rt.rtYearNote: RT page showed 1963 (US release). WARNING: rottentomatoes.com/m/stray_dog is a different 2015 film; use the 1020312 slug.

films.rationale: An early police procedural set in sweltering post-war Tokyo whose pairing of a young detective with an older mentor, played by Toshiro Mifune and Takashi Shimura, shaped later crime cinema.

films.title: Ran
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay).
films.rationale: King Lear transposed to warring-states Japan, with colour-coded armies and a battle scored without diegetic sound: a late-career summation of his scale and tragic vision.

films.title: Yojimbo
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay).
films.rationale: A wry, widescreen-composed genre dismantling that fused samurai and western tropes and became the source for A Fistful of Dollars.

films.title: Red Beard
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay).

rt.rtYearNote: 73% corroborated by the Kurosawa celebrity table; the review count of 15 comes from the film page only and is a thin sample. Dersu Uzala showed an identical 73% / 15 on the same fetcher: spot-check both by hand.

films.rationale: A three-hour humanist capstone to the Mifune partnership, set in a rural clinic; the closest call in the ten, kept over Kagemusha and Sanjuro because its directing ambition and audience standing outweigh its thin and mixed critic sample.

films.title: The Hidden Fortress
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew; screenplay credited to Hideo Oguni, Ryuzo Kikushima, Shinobu Hashimoto and Kurosawa.
alternateTitles: Three Bad Men in a Hidden Fortress

rt.rtYearNote: RT page showed 1962 (US release); its celebrity table and TMDB show 1958.

films.rationale: His first widescreen adventure: a brisk, funny chase told partly through two bickering peasants, and an acknowledged influence on Star Wars.

films.title: Throne of Blood
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay).
films.rationale: Macbeth recast through Noh theatre, fog and stylised movement, ending in one of cinema's most celebrated death scenes.

nearMisses.title: Kagemusha
nearMisses.reason: Palme d'Or (shared) but weaker evidence than Red Beard and overlaps with Ran.

nearMisses.title: Sanjuro
nearMisses.reason: Excellent but a sequel that restates Yojimbo.

nearMisses.title: Dersu Uzala
nearMisses.reason: Oscar winner, but outside the core Japanese-language body of work and thin critic sample.

nearMisses.title: Drunken Angel
nearMisses.reason: First Mifune collaboration; surpassed by Stray Dog.

nearMisses.title: The Bad Sleep Well
nearMisses.reason: Strong; no clear case against the chosen ten.

unverified: IMDb ids were matched from the IMDb dataset by original title, year and runtime, not read from a TMDB external-ids field (TMDB film pages show no IMDb link). Hidden Fortress runtime differs (TMDB 139 min, IMDb 126 min, a known shorter cut) and High and Low / Throne of Blood differ by 1-2 minutes; the matches are still correct but should be confirmed against the TMDB API external_ids at implementation.
RT review counts are a single read on the stated date via a text fetcher; Red Beard (73% / 15) in particular should be confirmed by hand.
IMDb title pages could not be read (HTTP 403); ratings are from the official dataset (not cross-checked against the live title pages), whose licence is non-commercial only.
